name: Petr Yan
summary: Bantamweight champion (20-5) on a four-fight win streak, all decisions, capped by a 25-minute win over Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 323. A patient, powerful boxer-wrestler who builds through rounds with body work and heavy rights. Returns from a major back operation after 10+ months out.

how_they_fight.Striking: Compact boxing behind a high guard, feints and switch-stance; heavy right hand and a punishing body attack. Against Dvalishvili in December his most effective weapon was body kicks and punches (POST Wrestling). About 5.6 significant strikes a minute at 60%.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Excellent takedown defence (about 86%): stuffed more than two dozen Dvalishvili attempts in the rematch, per POST Wrestling, and scored takedowns of his own. Uses trips and bodylocks on the fence; nearly finished McGhee with a kimura.
how_they_fight.Defense: Never stopped in 25 fights (verified). Absorbs about 3.8 strikes a minute and gives up early volume while he reads opponents. Was taken down and controlled for long spells in the first Dvalishvili fight (2023).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Classic slow starter and late finisher. Per Cageside Press he 'started slowly, as he often does' vs McGhee before hurting him late in R1 and in R2; CBS described him growing stronger each round vs Dvalishvili. Finishes (verified): R1 x3, R2 x1, R3 x3, R5 x1 (Aldo, 2020); 12 of 20 wins are decisions and he has not finished anyone since 2020. Losses: four decisions (three split) and a DQ for an illegal knee (Sterling R4, 2021).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: High: reads patterns over the first round and adjusts; the illegal knee on a downed Sterling shows aggression can override discipline. Has said he will target Dvalishvili's often-broken nose (MMA Sucka).

patterns: Slow first round, takes over from late R1/R2
Stuffs takedowns and makes wrestlers pay with power shots
UFC five-round fights: 4-3 (wins Aldo KO R5, Sandhagen, Figueiredo, Dvalishvili 2; losses Sterling DQ/S-DEC, Dvalishvili 1)
concerns: Coming off a nine-hour lumbar disc surgery (LowKick MMA; another report called it minor) and an inactive stretch since Dec. 2025
Early volume can cost him close rounds (three split-decision losses)
Lost a one-sided decision to Dvalishvili in 2023 when he couldn't stop the chain wrestling
keys_to_beat: Bank the early rounds with volume before he warms up
Test the back early with constant level changes and fence work
Avoid standing in front of him late; his power grows as opponents slow

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 135 lb (Dvalishvili 135). Bantamweight title fight confirmed.
Sherdog preview: -175 favourite (Dvalishvili +145); picks him by decision, crediting his improved takedown defence and late pressure.
Media day: 'I have a plan, and my plan is to come out there and win'; wants to finish the rivalry and 'turn the page'. Also criticised the UFC's push of Sean O'Malley. No new health news.
Posted his first training video since a nine-hour back surgery to repair damaged lumbar discs, done after UFC 323 (LowKick MMA). Sources disagree on how serious the operation was.
Says he will target and break Dvalishvili's nose.
Picks Volkanovski over fellow Russian Evloev 55/45; says he may move up to 145 but not while friend Volkanovski is champion.
Opened a -166 favourite over Dvalishvili (+140) at DraftKings.
